Question 1

In a trigonometry test, the class instructor decided that students whose z-score is greater than or equal to −1 will pass the test. The mean percent score x of the students of the class is x¯=64.3% with a standard deviation of σ=5.25%. Find the minimum passing score.

a
63.3%
b
59.05%
c
65.3%
d
61.3%
e
57.55%
Submit

decision.explanation: Using z=(x−64.3)/5.25, the minimum passing score occurs at z=−1: x=64.3−5.25=59.05%.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: In a trigonometry test, the class instructor decided that students whose $z$-score is greater than or equal to $-1$ will pass the test. The mean percent score $x$ of the students of the class is $\overset{¯}{x}=64.3%$ with a standard deviation of $\sigma =5.25%.$ Find the minimum passing score.
after.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

Substituting $\overset{―}{x}=64.3,$ $z=-1,$ and $\sigma =5.25$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\  & =64.3+(-1)\cdot 5.25 \\  & =64.3-5.25 \\  & =59.05.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the minimum passing score is $59.05%.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A data set contains the observations ${x}_{1}=28,{x}_{2}=18$ with $z$-scores ${z}_{1}=3.6$ and ${z}_{2}=1.1,$ respectively. Find the mean of the data set.
after.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+1.1\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the second equation from the first and solving for $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(28-18) & =(3.6-1.1)\cdot \sigma  \\ 10 & =2.5\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this value back into our first equation and solving for $\overset{¯}{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot \sigma  \\ 28 & =\overset{¯}{x}+3.6\cdot 4 \\ \overset{¯}{x} & =13.6.\end{aligned}
$$

x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma
